title: Reducedness after the first root extension tests geometric reducedness of a field
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p$, and choose an algebraic closure $\overline k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Put $k^{1/p}=\{x\in\overline k:x^p\in k\}$. Let $F/k$ be any field extension. For fields over $k$, use the scalar tensor product [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$ and unit $1\otimes1$. If $F\otimes_k k^{1/p}$ is reduced, then $F\otimes_k E$ is reduced for every field extension $E/k$. Reduced means that $x^m=0$ for an integer $m\ge1$ implies $x=0$. No algebraicity or finite-generation hypothesis on $F/k$, $E/k$ or $k^{1/p}/k$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 030W, label lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, equivalence of conditions (3) and (4), read at lines 10360–10407; geometric reducedness is expanded as its field-base-change meaning.

proof.text: Write $L=k^{1/p}$. The field operations preserve $L$: for $u,v\in L$, Frobenius gives $(u+v)^p=u^p+v^p$, $(uv)^p=u^pv^p$, and $(u^{-1})^p=(u^p)^{-1}$ when $u\ne0$; also $k\subseteq L$. For every $c\in k$, the polynomial $X^p-c$ has a root $r\in\overline k$, which belongs to $L$ and satisfies $r^p=c$. Put $Q=F\otimes_kL$. It has $p\cdot1=0$ since $p(1\otimes1)=(p\cdot1)\otimes1=0$.

source.place: Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, paragraph before the statement and the start of (3) implies (2).

proof.text: Let $b_1,\ldots,b_m\in F$ be linearly independent over $k$, and suppose $\sum_i c_ib_i^p=0$ with $c_i\in k$. Choose $r_i\in L$ with $r_i^p=c_i$ by step 1 and put $x=\sum_i b_i\otimes r_i\in Q$. Frobenius in $Q$ and tensor balancing give $$x^p=\sum_i b_i^p\otimes r_i^p=\sum_i c_ib_i^p\otimes1=0.$$ As $Q$ is reduced and $p\geq1$, $x=0$.

source.place: Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, (3) implies (2), the displayed formula for the homomorphism m and its Frobenius identity.

proof.text: Extend $\{b_1,\ldots,b_m\}$ to a $k$-basis of $F$ by the basis-extension node. The scalar-extension node says that its tensors with $1$ form an $L$-basis of $Q$. Thus $0=x=\sum_i r_i(b_i\otimes1)$ forces every $r_i=0$, hence every $c_i=r_i^p=0$. Therefore taking $p$-th powers preserves every finite $k$-linearly independent family in $F$. The empty family is included.

source.place: Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, (3) implies (2), independence of the scalar-extended family.

proof.text: Let $F_0$ be any intermediate field $k\subseteq F_0\subseteq F$ finitely generated as a field over $k$. A finite family in $F_0$ is $k$-linearly independent exactly when its image in $F$ is, since the inclusion is injective. Powers commute with this inclusion. Step 3 therefore gives the p-power independence hypothesis for $F_0$. Apply the cited finitely generated criterion to conclude that $F_0/k$ is separably generated.

Fix an arbitrary field extension $E/k$. It is reduced: if $e^n=0$ and $e\ne0$, multiplying by $(e^{-1})^n$ gives $1=0$. For every finitely generated intermediate field $F_0$ as in step 4, apply the separably-generated tensor-reducedness node with $K=F_0$ and $S=E$. Its hypotheses are precisely the separable generation just proved and this reducedness of $E$; hence $F_0\otimes_kE$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, (1) implies (4), using Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, separably generated case.

proof.text: Let $z\in F\otimes_kE$ and $n\geq1$ satisfy $z^n=0$. Write $z=\sum_{i=1}^s f_i\otimes e_i$ and put $F_0=k(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq F$. The inclusion $F_0\hookrightarrow F$ is injective and $k$-linear. The field-flatness node makes $E$ flat over $k$, so the definition of flatness gives an injective map $j:F_0\otimes_kE\to F\otimes_kE$. The tensor formulas show that $j$ preserves products. Set $z_0=\sum_i f_i\otimes e_i$ in its source. Then $j(z_0^n)=z^n=0$, so $z_0^n=0$. Step 5 gives $z_0=0$, whence $z=j(z_0)=0$. This includes $s=0$, where $F_0=k$. No finiteness of $F/k$ or $E/k$ was used.

source.place: Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, reduction to finitely generated field extensions; finite-support argument written explicitly, as used in Tag 030W (1) implies (4).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-e4835243b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full against Stacks algebra.tex Tag 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, lines 10360-10407): the item is (3)=>(4) with geometric reducedness spelled out as reducedness of F⊗E for every field extension E/k, not weakened, and the statement is unchanged. All 6 steps are correct. Step 1: L=k^{1/p} is a field and Q has p=0 (Frobenius, algebraic closure). Step 2: x^p=(Σc_i b_i^p)⊗1=0, so x=0 because Q is reduced. Step 3: the basis is extended and (b_j⊗1) is an L-basis (both are in the cited statements), so r_i=0 and c_i=0. Step 4: for every finitely generated F_0⊆F, the hypotheses of the Mathlib-leaf p-power criterion are checked, giving separable generation. Step 5: lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced is applied with S=E, a field and so reduced. Step 6: since E is flat, F_0⊗E→F⊗E is injective and multiplicative, which brings z^n=0 back to F_0⊗E. Every non-elementary use cites a node whose statement says it (C3/C4 ok). Edge cases checked: F=k, perfect k, k(t), s=0, and the inseparable case F_p(t)(t^{1/p}), where the hypothesis correctly fails. No new nodes. Duplicate search on 030W and k^{1/p} found only the converse and finite variants. Mathlib has no first-root criterion. The tool_use of lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced (unit sk-thm-p1, Lean-closed in slopmaster2) is accepted. No fixes.
